title: webAI Open-Sources TwIL-8B AI Model to Rival Frontier Performance Benchmarks
summary:
The new open-weight AI model from webAI scored 93% of frontier performance on coding, 92% on instruction following, and 90% on contest mathematics. Designed to run on personal hardware, the compact size of the model is intended to provide an alternative to the expensive API calls required by larger, proprietary language models.

The company's release of TwIL-8B, which utilizes 8.8B parameters, is part of a broader strategy to prioritize the efficiency and cost of completing tasks over the absolute size of the model. David Stout, who announced the launch via Hugging Face, said the goal is to create a future where intelligence can be specialized and distributed across existing user hardware.

selectedTweets.text:
Modest intelligence is arriving faster than most people realize.

Today, we're open-sourcing TwIL-8B.

Just 8.8 billion parameters, yet approaching frontier-model scores on several difficult benchmarks:

• 93% of frontier performance on coding

• 92% on instruction following

• 90% on contest mathematics

All from a model small enough to run on your own hardware.

But the benchmarks aren't the most important part of this announcement.

For years, the AI industry has focused on building the most capable model, regardless of the cost required to run it.

I believe that equation is changing.

The next era of AI will be defined by the cost of completing work. Not simply the intelligence of the model, but how efficiently that intelligence can accomplish the task.

If a model with 8 billion parameters can reliably complete the same work as one with hundreds of billions, why pay for the larger model?

As smaller models become more capable, intelligence becomes something we can distribute, specialize, and run across the hardware we already own.

That's the future we're building at @thewebAI 

TwIL-8B is available today. Open weights.

And this is just the first of several announcements we're making today.
